intro: Nothing on this site can choose a route for you until these questions are answered. Each one lists what is already known from official sources, what is missing, and a concrete way to obtain the missing fact. Questions are ordered by how much they change the answer.

questions.question: Are you a Chinese national, a foreign national, or a former Chinese national who has taken US citizenship?
questions.why: This single fact decides whether the USD 50,000 annual quota, the documented-income route, or the emigrant property transfer is even available.
questions.known: Domestic individuals get a USD 50,000 per year facilitation quota [S08 Art.2]. A foreign individual's China-source RMB income can be purchased with identity document plus source and tax documents [S08 Art.13, S10]; only permanent-residence holders get the annual quota [S11]. The emigrant route requires foreign permanent residence or citizenship plus cancelled mainland household registration [S14].
questions.missing: Your current nationality, household registration status, and whether you ever held a mainland hukou.
questions.how: Check your passport, your 户口簿 or its cancellation stamp, and any 注销户口证明. If you naturalised in the US, the cancellation certificate is the document SAFE asks for [S14].

questions.question: Where do you live for tax purposes now, and how many days were you in China this year?
questions.why: China taxes residents on worldwide income after 183 days, and the US taxes citizens on worldwide income regardless of residence. The overlap decides whether a foreign tax credit is available and whether the foreign earned income exclusion applies.
questions.known: China: resident if domiciled or present 183+ days, taxed on worldwide income, with a credit for foreign tax paid [S20 Art.1, Art.7]. US: foreign earned income exclusion needs a foreign tax home plus bona fide residence or 330 days abroad [S25]; exclusion for 2027 is USD 137,300 [S26].
questions.missing: Your day count, your tax home, and whether you claim the exclusion on Form 2555.
questions.how: Pull entry and exit records from both passports and count days; keep the count with your return file.

questions.question: What is the exact balance, and how did each part of it arise?
questions.why: Conversion cost is proportional to the balance, and the documentation you can produce depends on whether the money is salary, a property sale, a gift, or accumulated interest.
questions.known: Different document sets are prescribed for salary, business income, capital income, property transfer and incidental income, plus an original tax certificate [S14].
questions.missing: Balance, currency composition, and a line-by-line origin for each deposit.
questions.how: Download 12-24 months of statements and tax payment records from the bank app; match each large credit to a contract, payslip, sale deed or dividend notice.

questions.question: Was PRC individual income tax already paid on the income that produced this balance?
questions.why: The conversion itself is not a taxable event, but unpaid PRC tax on the source income is the one thing that can turn a bank visit into a penalty case.
questions.known: Rates: comprehensive income 3%-45%, business income 5%-35%, interest, dividends, property transfer and incidental income 20% [S20 Art.3]. Late payment surcharge is 0.05% per day [S31 Art.32]. A taxpayer owing tax can be stopped from leaving China [S31 Art.44].
questions.missing: Whether a 完税证明 exists for each income stream, and whether any year is unfiled.
questions.how: Request a 个人所得税纳税记录 from the 个人所得税 app or the district tax office for each year the balance was earned.

questions.question: Have you filed FBARs and Forms 8938 for every year this account existed?
questions.why: An unreported account is a far larger financial risk than the conversion spread: the penalty can exceed the entire cost of converting.
questions.known: FBAR required when aggregate foreign accounts exceed USD 10,000 at any point [S21]. Non-willful penalty USD 16,536; willful USD 165,353 [S22]. Form 8938 thresholds and a USD 10,000 penalty rising by up to USD 50,000 [S23]. Streamlined procedures exist for non-willful failures [S30].
questions.missing: A year-by-year filing history and the peak balance in each year.
questions.how: Pull IRS account transcripts for the last six years and compare against bank year-end and peak balances.

questions.question: What is your basis in the CNY, in USD?
questions.why: The US taxes the currency gain on conversion, not the conversion itself. Without a documented USD basis you cannot compute the gain, and the exclusion is only USD 200.
questions.known: Disposing of nonfunctional currency is a section 988 transaction, gain is ordinary, and the personal-transaction exclusion covers only the first USD 200 of gain [S27]. The IRS publishes yearly average rates (China 2025: 7.129; 2024: 7.189) [S07].
questions.missing: The USD value of the CNY at the time each deposit was received.
questions.how: Convert each deposit at the rate on the day received, or at the IRS yearly average if used consistently [S07], and keep the worksheet.

questions.question: How much do you need to move, and by when?
questions.why: Size decides which route is cheapest. Under about USD 21,000 the HSBC Premier route is cheapest in the model; above that the BOC wire is. Timing decides whether the USD 50,000 annual quota can be used across two calendar years.
questions.known: Cost rows are computed for every USD 10,000 increment to USD 400,000 and the cheapest priced route is marked in each row [model].
questions.how: Pick the row in the cost table that matches your amount; if the deadline allows, split across two calendar years to use two annual quotas [S08 Art.2].

questions.question: Which banks do you actually hold accounts with, in China and in the US?
questions.why: The cheapest route in the model requires either a BOC mainland account or an HSBC pair, and HSBC Premier requires a CNY 500,000 relationship balance.
questions.known: BOC wire: 0.1% capped at CNY 260 plus CNY 150 cable [S03]. HSBC: 0.1% capped at CNY 500 plus CNY 120 cable, or free by Global Transfer for Premier [S04]. Premier carries CNY 300 per month below CNY 500,000 [S04].
questions.missing: Your account list and current balances.
questions.how: Log into each bank and note account type, currency and balance; if you have HSBC in both countries, check whether you qualify for Premier.

questions.question: What do the correspondent and receiving banks actually charge on your route?
questions.why: Both published fee schedules stop at the sending bank. The landing amount can be lower than the estimate.
questions.known: The BOC and HSBC pages read state the sending-bank fee only; correspondent and receiving charges are additional [S03, S04].
questions.missing: A real remittance advice showing the amount credited.
questions.how: Send one small test transfer (for example USD 1,000) and read the credited amount; use the difference as the true all-in cost.

questions.question: Does the bank apply the board rate or a different internal rate to this product?
questions.why: The cost table uses the published board rate. If a product applies a different rate, the spread changes and every row moves.
questions.known: Board rates are published and are stated to be for reference only; the actual transaction rate applies [S01]. The HSBC tariff does not state the conversion pricing for Global Transfer [S04].
questions.missing: The rate actually applied on a Global Transfer or on a large wire.
questions.how: Ask the branch in writing for the rate applied to your product, or read the rate on the confirmation of a test transfer.

questions.question: Will you be claiming the foreign earned income exclusion, or the foreign tax credit, or both?
questions.why: You cannot take a credit for tax on income you excluded, so the choice changes the net cost of the whole exercise.
questions.known: The credit is only for foreign income, war profits and excess profits taxes, and no credit is allowed for tax on excluded income [S29]. Exclusion for 2026 is USD 132,900 and for 2027 USD 137,300 [S26].
questions.missing: Your US taxable income and the PRC tax actually paid per year.
questions.how: Model both on Form 1116 and Form 2555 with your last return; the higher of the two results is the one to claim.

questions.question: Is any part of the balance a gift from a relative, or an inheritance?
questions.why: A gift is reported on Form 3520 above USD 100,000 but is generally not taxable, and it may not be convertible through the salary route.
questions.known: Form 3520 Part IV is required above USD 100,000 aggregate from a nonresident alien in a year, with each gift above USD 5,000 identified [S24].
questions.missing: Whether any credit into the account was a gift, and from whom.
questions.how: Match large credits to gift deeds or transfer records; if none, treat as income and document it as such.

questions.question: Has the account ever been flagged, restricted, or placed on a watch list?
questions.why: A prior flag changes what the bank will accept and can add two years of strict review.
questions.known: Individuals who borrow or lend quota, or split purchases, are placed on a watch list with strict review for two years [S15]. Exceeding the overseas cash withdrawal cap suspends the card function for two years [S16].
questions.missing: Any notice from the bank or SAFE.
questions.how: Ask the bank for the account status in writing and keep the reply.

questions.question: If the route needs an approval, how long will it take and what will it cost in professional time?
questions.why: The emigrant route has no SAFE fee but needs a full documentary chain, which usually means paid help.
questions.known: No fee is charged by SAFE; decision within 20 working days, extendable once by 10 [S14]. Filing is on site only [S14].
questions.missing: Whether you qualify, and what a local agent or lawyer would charge.
questions.how: Ask the local SAFE branch and two local agents for a written quote and checklist before starting.

questions.question: Do you have a USD 10,000-plus cash movement planned that requires a US customs filing?
questions.why: Carrying cash is one of the priced routes, and failing to declare it can cost more than the transfer.
questions.known: FinCEN Form 105 is required above USD 10,000 entering or leaving the US; failure risks forfeiture and civil or criminal penalties [S28].
questions.missing: Whether any route you choose involves physical cash.
questions.how: If it does, pre-fill Form 105 before travel and keep the receipt.
